story.what_it_does: Supreme Industries is India's largest plastic pipes and products maker, also selling value-added items such as CPVC pipes, furniture, industrial components and windows. In FY2025-26 it sold about 753,907 MT, up about 12% in volume, with revenue from operations of about ₹11,218 crore.
story.plans: Management plans about ₹1,000 crore of capex in FY2026-27 (later guided to ₹700 crore), funded from internal accruals, and wants capacity of 1.5 million MT by 2027-28. It also expects the Jammu and Patna units to be commissioned in 2026-27 and is building out windows and gas piping.
story.moat: The notes describe it as the largest plastic pipes processor, with about 13% piping market share and about 25% return on capital employed over 18 years. It is debt free with a cash surplus of ₹685 crore at 30 Sep 2026, which helps it fund expansion itself, but raw material costs follow crude oil and polymer prices.

scenarios.story: Volumes recover as polymer prices settle and new capacity comes online, with October 2026 volume up about 23% so far. Value-added products and the cash surplus support the 14% margin guidance.
signals_to_watch: Piping volume growth versus the 13% FY27 guidance after the weak first half
Operating margin holding at about 14% for FY27

scenarios.story: Volumes grow roughly 10% company-wide in FY27 with margins near 14%, as management guides. Revenue reaches at least ₹13,500 crore, with polymer price swings continuing to cause noise.
signals_to_watch: Company-wide volume growth of about 10% for FY27
Revenue of at least ₹13,500 crore for FY27

scenarios.story: Polymer price volatility and geopolitical uncertainty keep hurting demand, and guidance is cut again after earlier cuts. Industrial and consumer products stay weak and government-linked orders fall short.
signals_to_watch: Nal Se Jal orders coming in much lower than budget
Margins missing estimates again because of polymer cost pressure
